title: A standard projective-bundle fibre with its normalized line
statement: Let S be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], E a quasi-coherent finite locally free module of rank r>=2 [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module], D a normalized tautological quotient for its canonical symmetric relative Proj [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry], and s a point of S. Write p:P(E)->S and i_s:p.fiber(s)->P(E) for the scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. There is an isomorphism e from standard projective space with r homogeneous coordinates over Spec kappa(s) to p.fiber(s), such that e^* i_s^* D.line is isomorphic to the standard O(1) [def-pc-projective-space-twist], using tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. This asserts no classification of arbitrary invertible modules and no comparison of higher powers.

source.place: Tags 01OA and 01OE, section-projective-bundle and example-projective-space; lemma-relative-proj-base-change, Tag 01O3.

proof.text: Choose a local rank-r frame of E at s. Pull it to Spec kappa(s). The resulting vector space E_s is free with exactly r basis vectors. Symmetric algebra commutes with this base change and sends the chosen basis to the standard polynomial generators; the maps preserve degree since they do so on the degree-one generators.

source.place: Tags 01OA and 01OE, section-projective-bundle and example-projective-space; lemma-relative-proj-base-change, Tag 01O3.

proof.text: Relative-Proj base change identifies the fibre with Proj of this residue-field symmetric algebra. The ordered basis identifies this with standard projective space with r coordinates. Equivalently this follows by representing the same rank-one quotients; invert the comparison to obtain e from standard projective space to the fibre.

source.place: Tags 01OA and 01OE, section-projective-bundle and example-projective-space; lemma-relative-proj-base-change, Tag 01O3.

proof.text: The normalization of D.chart identifies D.line with the degree-one relative-Proj twist on each affine base chart. Under the coefficientwise base-change and ordered polynomial comparisons its standard frame is T_i, and its transitions are T_i/T_j. The comparisons thus give isomorphisms with O(1) on every standard chart, agreeing on overlaps. Glue these isomorphisms and their inverses, using tensor-pullback composition to identify the twice-pulled-back line in the statement. This argument compares the given D, rather than a separately chosen quotient.

theorem exists_projective_bundle_fiber_twist_model (S : Scheme.{u}) (E : S.Modules)
    [E.IsQuasicoherent] (r : ℕ)
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E r] (hr : 2 ≤ r)
    (D : TautologicalQuotient E) (s : S) :
    ∃ e : ℙ(ULift.{u} (Fin r); Spec (.of (S.residueField s))) ≅
        (SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProjHom.fiber s,
      Nonempty
        ((tensorPullback e.hom).obj
          ((tensorPullback
            ((SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProjHom.fiberι s)).obj D.line) ≅
          ProjectiveSpace.twist (ULift.{u} (Fin r)) (Spec (.of (S.residueField s))) 1)
